body.x: Ceragem participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas, unveiling its vision for the “AI Wellness Home (Alive Intelligence Wellness Home).”

Under the theme “a living, breathing home that knows me best,” Ceragem welcomed global visitors with an AI Wellness Home concept booth. The company explained that it expanded the concept of “My Future Home,” introduced at last year’s CES, to encompass the entire house, presenting a new direction for home healthcare in which the home itself operates as a comprehensive health management platform.

While conventional AI homes have focused on automating household appliances around functional convenience, Ceragem’s AI Wellness Home extends the concept into healthcare, presenting a lifestyle-oriented residential model. By integrating lifestyle patterns, health data, and daily rhythms, Ceragem differentiated its approach with an integrated healthcare platform that enables health management to occur naturally in everyday life.

Based on its so-called “7-Care Solution,” Ceragem reconfigured home spaces to reflect generational lifestyles and health needs—from growth stages through adulthood to senior years—proposing a residential health platform in which personalized healthcare is organically integrated throughout daily living.

body.cap: “Brain Booth with AI Coach” displayed in the Clarity & Recharge Zone | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Ceragem organized its exhibition into three lifestyle zones: the Clarity & Recharge Zone, the Everyday Vitality Zone, and the Serenity & Care Zone. Through this structure, the company emphasized that it envisioned the AI Wellness Home expanding with age and lifestyle.

The Clarity & Recharge Zone focused on the formative lifestyles of teens and young adults, designing an environment where emotional stability and learning are managed as a continuous flow. Products on display included the “Youth Bed with AI Health Concierge,” which supports growth and recovery; the “Brain Booth with AI Coach” for optimized learning environments; “Balance Air” to support air circulation; and the relaxation device “Pause M6.” These products were designed to deliver personalized care based on users’ daily data.

The Everyday Vitality Zone was implemented as a living-centered space that helps users maintain a healthy balance. Targeting the lifestyles of people in their 40s and 50s—where work, rest, and self-care intersect—the zone connected health management with recovery.

body.cap: Everyday Vitality Zone inside the Ceragem booth | Photo by AVING News

body.x: This area featured the “Master AI Multi Therapy Pod,” which offers customized programs; home beauty devices “Medispa Pro” and “All-in-One”; the high-end sauna booth “Therapier (Home Therapies)” providing personalized multi-sensory therapy; and the “Balance AI Shower System,” which analyzes skin condition and automatically delivers tailored solutions. Together, these offerings presented an integrated wellness experience built around the 7-Care Solution.

Designed for seniors in their 70s and 80s, the Serenity & Care Zone was introduced as a space that considers blood circulation management, daily recovery, and emotional stability associated with aging. Exhibits included the “Celtron Chair” medical device for improving blood circulation, “Balance Mediwater AI,” which supports customized hydration, nutrition, and medication habits, the depression-care medical device “Mind Fit,” and a home medical care bed.

Ceragem also set up a dedicated “CERACHECK” zone to present its personalized healthcare platform, introducing visitors to its vision of a system that connects the entire health management process—from measurement and analysis to customized care.

A Ceragem representative said, “At CES 2026, Ceragem sought to show how AI can evolve beyond a simple technology into a presence that understands and accompanies users in everyday life,” adding, “The AI Wellness Home will become a new standard in which the home itself designs and completes health.”
